name: Regime-arm requires a fresh macro TURN (regime cross_up, not a static level gate)
rationale: THESIS: The most informative moment is not BEING in a risk-on regime — it is the macro composite TURNING risk-on, because the regime-transition is when growth-beta re-rates and trend has the most runway ahead. A static level gate (macro_regime>floor) keeps you long deep into a stale, already-priced regime where forward edge is gone. Instead I require the macro composite to have freshly crossed UP through its floor recently, then arm the trend. macro_regime is BOUNDED so cross_up on its level is a legitimate transition signal (not a drifting-feature abuse — the composite is mean-bounded). Entry: macro_regime cross_up regime_floor AND ret_Nd>mom_floor. DISCONFIRMER: run the SAME momentum entry but with macro_regime as a STATIC gt level gate (always-in-regime) instead of the fresh cross_up. If the always-in version reproduces the cross_up version's net-of-fee Sharpe, the freshness of the macro TURN carries no info and this is a plain level gate — falsified. The turn-timing must add edge over static membership.
catalyst: Macro composite freshly crosses up through its risk-on floor (a regime transition) while a trend is positive — the re-rating window arms momentum at its highest-runway moment.
